title: kayaknya, sepertinya, mungkin
pattern: Sepertinya … / Kayaknya … (it looks like) · Mungkin … (maybe) · Kira-kira … (about, roughly)
explanation: To guess, or to soften what you say, put one of these at the front of the sentence. sepertinya means it looks like, it seems, from what you can see or tell: Sepertinya mau hujan (Looks like it's going to rain). kayaknya is the same word in casual speech, and you'll hear it constantly among friends: Kayaknya dia capek (He seems tired). mungkin is maybe or probably, a guess with less to go on: Mungkin dia lupa (Maybe she forgot). kira-kira is about or roughly, for numbers and times (kira-kira jam tujuh, around seven), and it softens a question: Kira-kira berapa lama? (About how long, do you think?).
natural: These are how Indonesians say no without quite saying it: Sepertinya saya tidak bisa datang (I don't think I can come) is kinder than Saya tidak bisa datang. Kira-kira makes a question to a driver or a shopkeeper sound less demanding.
stiff: kayaknya is casual: with someone older or at work, use sepertinya. And when someone answers your invitation with just mungkin, it may well be a polite no.

examples.english: It looks like it's going to rain.

gap.why: A guess from what you can see, like dark clouds: sepertinya. Katanya would mean someone told you.

examples.registerNotes: Mau here is 'about to', not 'want': mau hujan, it's going to rain.

examples.indonesian: Mungkin dia lupa. Coba telepon lagi.
examples.english: Maybe she forgot. Try calling again.

gap.why: A guess with not much to go on: mungkin, 'maybe'.

examples.indonesian: Kayaknya aku nggak bisa ikut, deh.
examples.english: I don't think I can make it.

gap.note: Sepertinya works too; next to aku and nggak, the casual kayaknya fits better.
gap.why: Starting with kayaknya turns a flat no into 'I don't think I can'.

examples.registerNotes: Casual, to a friend. Politely: Maaf, sepertinya saya tidak bisa ikut.

examples.english: About what time will you get here?

gap.why: For a rough time or number, kira-kira: 'about, roughly'.

examples.registerNotes: Kira-kira takes the pressure off: he doesn't have to know exactly.
